notes: This records an owner decision to stop treating native UI automation as a release gate. It is NOT a statement that native UI tests passed.

Certification and promotion must represent this as NOT_REQUIRED_BY_CURRENT_POLICY. Representing it as PASS would assert coverage that does not exist; representing it as BLOCKED or OPERATIONAL_FAILURE would assert a failure that is not being measured.

Six consecutive live dispatches produced no usable flow evidence. Every failure traced to test infrastructure -- runner image, Xcode scheme selection, shell dialect, and JS bundling -- rather than to the application under test.
No replacement runner is selected in this pass. Choosing one is deliberately out of scope so the decision is not made under schedule pressure.
reinstatement_requires: A replacement runner selected intentionally, not inherited by default.
Reliable operation on both supported mobile platforms, or explicit per-platform runners with their own policy entries.
Flows that exercise real application behavior rather than placeholder assertions, verified against the product surface each flow ID claims.
Evidence bound to the exact candidate SHA.
Genuine application failures classified as BLOCKED.
Several consecutive successful CI validations before the control becomes release-blocking again.
reinstatement_procedure: Set status to ACTIVE and required_for_release to true in this file. Certification and promotion read this policy at runtime, so no code change is needed to re-arm the gate.
